source.title: The interplay between randomness and structure during learning in RNNs
source.authors: Friedrich Schuessler; Francesca Mastrogiuseppe; A. Dubreuil; S. Ostojic; O. Barak

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary information are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains recurrent networks from random initialization and reports task loss and validation accuracy, but does not test the claim versions’ convolutional classification, width, depth, or initialization conditions.
record.gate_note: The reported RNN task outcomes bear on gradient-based training from random initialization. The paper does not report CIFAR classification error, random-label training, or any of the specific interventions in V1–V6. Singular values and convergence-time measurements are not independent rows unless tied to a reported training outcome.
record.test_reason: The study measures convergence, initialization effects and low-rank weight changes in recurrent networks. None tests V1–V6: its initialization comparisons concern recurrent connectivity amplification and available learning directions, rather than activation-matched propagation across layers or trainable depth. Its divergence examples do not measure a learning-rate stability threshold or curvature.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find low-rank training-induced recurrent connectivity changes, explain accelerated learning through correlations with initial random connectivity in a simplified linear model, and demonstrate low-rank changes in an SST-2 LSTM. The LSTM observation depends on the training recipe: higher learning rates produced much higher effective rank.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies recurrent networks on neuroscience-inspired tasks and a linear input-output task, using quadratic task losses (and binary cross-entropy for SST-2); it does not study benchmark training classification error as specified in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initial connectivity strength g changes convergence time and, for flip-flop, functional rank. In the LSTM experiment, higher learning rates produced rugged curves, replacement of initial connectivity by ΔW, and higher effective rank; the authors state that other hyperparameters such as L2 regularization may also change the picture. For the linear task, large target amplitude with g = 0.8 caused gradient divergence and stopped learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Nonlinear RNNs converge on three neuroscience tasks. Nonzero initial recurrent connectivity accelerates learning, with convergence slowing again at sufficiently large g.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initial random recurrent connectivity can accelerate gradient-based task learning, with a nonmonotonic dependence on connectivity strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Low-rank truncations of learned recurrent weight changes preserve task performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-induced connectivity changes can be functionally low rank on the tested recurrent tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: In the simplified linear RNN, initial connectivity accelerates learning; first-order theory predicts convergence time proportional to (1 − g²)².
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random recurrent connectivity amplifies learned changes and reduces the effective learning time needed for the tested input-output mapping.

fits_no_version.finding: A large-target linear RNN diverges, and cosine learning fails without initial connectivity but produces slightly unstable solutions with nonzero connectivity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear RNN learning depends on available connectivity directions, target amplitude and recurrent dynamical stability.

fits_no_version.finding: For the SST-2 LSTM, truncating learned changes preserves accuracy at much lower rank than truncating full weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retaining initial weights while compressing their learned changes can preserve LSTM performance more efficiently than full-weight truncation in the tested recipe.

record.problems: Results use low-dimensional RNN tasks rather than the claim versions’ benchmark classification settings. Several outcomes are described qualitatively or shown in figures, and exact final task-loss or accuracy values are not provided in the text. The paper notes that higher learning rates and other hyperparameters can change the LSTM result.
record.rows_left_out: No additional outcome rows omitted. Figure-only numerical curves and singular-value measurements were not transcribed as outcomes because the text does not state their values and they do not independently measure task convergence or accuracy.

untested.parts: All: convolutional CIFAR training classification error, including corrupted labels and model-size or training-recipe comparisons.
All: two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and extra student neurons.
All: depth degradation, identity shortcuts and the stated alternative training recipes.
All: activation-matched initialization, propagation across layers, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights or convolution kernels.
All: learning-rate thresholds of the linearized model, curvature, catapult recovery and edge-of-stability training.
All: batch-normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance comparisons, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6 because all rows fall outside those versions; this does not negate the reported recurrent-network findings. Figure 5(b)'s validation-accuracy caption conflicts with Section 4's training-accuracy wording.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, corrupted or random labels, and the stated model-size, early-stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth effects, ImageNet/CIFAR-10 training error, and the stated special-initialization or normalization-free methods.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and very deep plain networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, sharpness, loss recovery, and divergence relative to those thresholds.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup normalization-free residual training.

rows.subject: two-layer LSTM

rows.note: The text reports training accuracy; the numeric accuracy is not stated.
rows.check: Change operation to post-training truncation. Figure 5(b) identifies validation accuracy, whereas Section 4 calls it training accuracy; flag this internal discrepancy. Rank-10 performance preservation does not establish near-zero training error.

rows.check: Full-weight truncation measures compression, outside V1–V6. Figure 5(b) identifies the plotted measure as validation accuracy.
